**Claim:** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat) — branch `claude/issue-6396-previousvalues-spread-hygiene`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in the same label write.

## Pre-dispatch gate

**1. Thread read.** Triage comment (19:53:46Z) read in full; its charter is the scope below, in order.
**2. Shadow check.** Nothing in flight — the queue drained and no dev is running. Batch-mates this round: **#6310** (`plugin-designer` + `i18n` locales) and **#6309** (`app-shell/metadata-admin/previews`). ⭐ Checked against **the batch as well as the in-flight set** — no overlap with `packages/components/src/renderers/form/`. Branch from current `main`.
**3. Premise.** The card measured it on `origin/main @ 631d81dbf`; `main` has moved many times since. ⛔ Re-derive the warning on the merged tree before fixing.

## Scope — triage's charter, and the fork is the whole point

**Step 1 — determine whether `previousValues` has a real consumer on the master-detail header path.** This is a measurement, not a formality, and it decides which of the next two you are allowed to do.

**Step 2 (if a consumer exists) — spread hygiene only.** Consume-and-drop before the DOM spread in `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` (it is already destructured at `:978-979`, with a comment pointing at objectui#3484 — read it). Pin that the warning is gone: assert **no unknown-prop stderr on a header render**.

**⛔ Step 3 (if NO consumer exists anywhere) — STOP. Do not delete the declared key as a rider.** Report it (`out_of_scope_findings`, or a fresh card) so the dead declared key goes through the **enforce-or-remove** channel with its own review.

⭐ **Triage drew the Clause-② line exactly, and it is the reason step 3 is a stop rather than a tidy-up:** the spread fix alone is **Clause-② no**; removing the declared key **changes the authorable surface** and is **Clause-② yes**. Those are different review tiers. A PR that quietly does both gets the second one reviewed as if it were the first.

⚠️ **#6033 covers only the zod-mirror census row.** This card is the **runtime leak**. Do not widen into #6033's territory.

Declared surface for reference: `packages/types/src/form.ts:1101` · `packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts:624`. ⛔ Neither is yours to change on this card.

## Tests

- ⛔ **Ghost-assertion guard (mandatory):** run the new assertion against unmodified `origin/main`, capture it **failing**, then passing. Both readings in the PR body.
- ⚠️ **The instrument is the hard part here.** The symptom is a `console.error` from React, not a thrown error or a DOM difference. An assertion that merely renders and passes proves nothing. Assert on **captured stderr/console output**, and prove the capture works by showing it catching the warning on unmodified `main`.
- ⛔ **Degenerate-control guard:** a render that never had the warning must still pass — otherwise you have pinned "no console output at all", which the next unrelated warning will break.

## Ground rules

Worktree-first: `git worktree add ../objectui-6396 -b claude/issue-6396-previousvalues-spread-hygiene main && cd ../objectui-6396 && pnpm install`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack lives in the common `.git` dir and is shared across every worktree of this repo. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Changeset: `patch`, per package changed. Run the repo's fast checks before pushing. Open the PR as **draft** with `Fixes #6396` and report back — the PM lands it, ⛔ never self-merge.

**If step 1 finds no consumer, a zero-implementation stop with the measurement is the correct and expected outcome** — not a failure.

Size: S. Model: opus.

**ACCEPT (pending green CI).** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`, `domain:ui` execution seat. Reviewed against the **tree**.

## Step 1 resolved the fork correctly — a real consumer exists, so this is step 2

Named precisely, not asserted: `form.tsx`'s `previousRecord` memo (`:979` destructures off `schema`; `:1140-1147` builds the record), which binds `previous` for field-rule CEL and supplies the INSERT/UPDATE signal the read-only submit strip gates on (objectui#3484). The producer is live too — `ObjectForm.tsx:1057` computes it for edit + `recordId`, and `MasterDetailForm.tsx:976` renders that `ObjectForm` as its header.

⇒ Step 3's stop was not triggered, the declared surface is untouched, **Clause-② no**. Correct branch of the charter.

## ⭐⭐ The leak was on a different channel than the card supposed

> `SchemaRenderer` spreads every non-metadata top-level schema key as a React prop **in addition to** passing `schema`, so the renderer got a second, top-level copy in `...props`.

`form.tsx:2531-2582` **already** consume-and-drops that whole family — `objectName`, `onDirtyChange`, `defaultValues`, `fields`, `layout`, … — and **`previousValues` was the one member missing from the list.**

Verified on the branch: the entire fix is one entry added to that existing drop-list, `previousValues: _previousValuesProp,` with the mechanism documented inline. 3 files, **+196 / −0**. The `schema` consumer never reads `props`, so it is provably unaffected.

⭐ **A one-line fix that took a real measurement to find is the good outcome, not a small one.** The obvious reading — "a declared key leaks, so stop declaring it or stop passing it" — would have gone after the wrong channel entirely and landed in Clause-② territory for no reason.

## ⚠️ The premise is worse than the card recorded

> React 19 not only declines the prop, it also stamps the element with `previousvalues="[object Object]"`, so the persisted record object was reaching the DOM as an attribute on **every edit-mode header render**.

Stringified, so no field values are exposed — the dev checked that and said so rather than leaving the reader to wonder. ⭐ **Re-deriving found the defect had grown since filing.** That is what "re-derive on the merged tree" is for; inheriting the card's description would have understated it.

## ⭐ Why every existing test missed it — and the instrument that catches it

The pin renders through **`SchemaRenderer`** (the host path) rather than off the registry, *"which is exactly why every existing `previousValues` test missed this — `<Form schema={…} />` never populates `...props`."*

A blind instrument identified by name, with the reason it was blind. The old tests were not weak; they were pointed at a path where the bug cannot occur.

The capture joins each `console.error` call's args, because React passes the prop name as a **separate `%s` argument**, not inside the format string — a detail that would silently produce a never-matching matcher.

## ⭐ Two controls, both green on both legs, both deliberate

- **Positive control** — renders a bare `<div madeUpProp>` and asserts the capture **does** catch a real unknown-prop warning, so a green pin cannot go vacuous if the capture breaks or React stops warning.
- **Degenerate control** — the same node **without** `previousValues` plus an unrelated `console.error`, asserting the pin still passes: the matcher requires `/does not recognize/` **and** the prop name, so it pins **one named prop, not silence.**

That second one is exactly what my dispatch order asked for. The positive control is beyond it, and it is the one that keeps this pin honest years from now.

Ghost guard both legs: on unmodified `origin/main` **2 failed / 2 passed** (the two controls being the two that pass), failing on the captured warning **and** on `form.getAttribute('previousvalues')` being `'[object Object]'` rather than null. After: 4 passed.

⭐ **Lint was a full repo-wide `eslint .` in one pass** — 3788 files, 0 errors — with the report stating plainly *"no narrowing argument relied on."* When the full run is affordable, running it beats arguing that the narrow one suffices.

⛔ **Not enqueued** — CI is 15 ✅ / 3 skip / 0 ❌ with **10 pending**. `in_progress` is not a verdict.
